records.reason: 5 \ 0.5 — VBA's \ (integer division) rounds each operand to a whole number first via banker's rounding (round-half-to-even), not truncation. 0.5 rounds to 0 (nearest even), giving 5 \ 0 — a real division by zero, matching real VBA, not a bug.
0.1 \ 0.2 — both operands round to 0 before the \ operator divides (0.1 and 0.2 are both closer to 0 than to 1), giving a real division by zero.
5 Mod 0.5 — same operand-rounding rule as \ applies to Mod. 0.5 rounds to 0 (nearest even), giving 5 Mod 0 — a real division by zero.
0.1 Mod 0.2 — both operands round to 0 before Mod divides, giving a real division by zero.
5 / 0 — a literal division by zero. Real VBA raises the same runtime error.
0 / 0 — a literal division by zero (indeterminate form still errors in real VBA, it does not produce NaN).

Application.WorksheetFunction.TextJoin — deliberately unimplemented worksheet function (this scenario's own category name is 'unsupported_functions'; it exists specifically to exercise the not-implemented path, not to pass).
Application.WorksheetFunction.Xlookup — deliberately unimplemented worksheet function, same reasoning as unsupported_functions_0001.

Timer() is not implemented. Its own category is 'nondeterministic' (time-dependent output would make this scenario unable to have a fixed expected value even if Timer() were implemented), so leaving it unimplemented is low-value to fix and the failure is registered rather than chased.
